## KMP-001: Shared declaration is named after one platform's key mechanism

Name shared `expect` declarations and interfaces after the intent, such as `storeToken(token, requiringUserAuth)`, and let each platform's `actual` pick the right primitive. Prefer an interface with injected implementations to `expect class`, which is still Beta.

```kotlin
// commonMain: say what you need, not how.
interface SecureTokenStore {
    suspend fun store(token: String, requireUserPresence: Boolean)
    suspend fun read(): String?          // null if absent or the user canceled
    suspend fun clear()
}

// androidMain: Keystore-backed key + Tink/DataStore (§6.6).
// iosMain: Keychain item with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly and,
//          when requireUserPresence is true, a SecAccessControl built from that class plus
//          .userPresence, passed as kSecAttrAccessControl in place of kSecAttrAccessible (§4.6).
```

Verify: List every `expect` declaration and shared interface that touches keys or tokens; each name should describe what the caller needs, not a platform API.

Book: [§21.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#212-the-mistake-that-will-bite-you)

## KMP-002: Platform crypto, keystore, or biometric API used in commonMain

Keep these calls in `androidMain` and `iosMain`. Put an intent-based interface in `commonMain` and inject each platform's implementation.

```kotlin
// commonMain: say what you need, not how.
interface SecureTokenStore {
    suspend fun store(token: String, requireUserPresence: Boolean)
    suspend fun read(): String?          // null if absent or the user canceled
    suspend fun clear()
}

// androidMain: Keystore-backed key + Tink/DataStore (§6.6).
// iosMain: Keychain item with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly and,
//          when requireUserPresence is true, a SecAccessControl built from that class plus
//          .userPresence, passed as kSecAttrAccessControl in place of kSecAttrAccessible (§4.6).
```

Verify: Search `commonMain` for `javax.crypto`, `java.security`, `android.security`, `androidx.biometric`, `platform.Security`, and `platform.LocalAuthentication`; nothing should remain.

Book: [§21.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#211-the-line-and-the-reasoning-behind-it)

## KMP-003: Ktor pins are shared, but an engine doesn't enforce them

Keep the pin strings in `commonMain`, and enforce them in each platform's `actual`: OkHttp's `CertificatePinner` on Android and the Darwin engine's `CertificatePinner` through `handleChallenge` on iOS. Put both in the same pull request.

```kotlin
// commonMain: the pins themselves are shared
object CertificatePins {
    const val HOST = "api.example.com"
    const val CURRENT = "sha256/YLh1dUR9y6Kja30RrAn7JKnbQG/uEtLMkBgFF2Fuihg="
    const val BACKUP = "sha256/Vjs8r4z+80wjNcr1YKepWQboSIRi63WsWXhIMN+eWys="
}

expect fun createPinnedHttpClient(): HttpClient

// iosMain: Darwin engine, with Ktor's own pinner. It validates the chain first by default.
import io.ktor.client.HttpClient
import io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.Darwin
import io.ktor.client.engine.darwin.certificates.CertificatePinner

actual fun createPinnedHttpClient(): HttpClient = HttpClient(Darwin) {
    engine {
        handleChallenge(
            CertificatePinner.Builder()
                .add(CertificatePins.HOST, CertificatePins.CURRENT, CertificatePins.BACKUP)
                .build()
        )
    }
}

// androidMain: OkHttp engine, so OkHttp's CertificatePinner applies
import io.ktor.client.engine.okhttp.OkHttp
import okhttp3.CertificatePinner

actual fun createPinnedHttpClient(): HttpClient = HttpClient(OkHttp) {
    engine {
        config {
            certificatePinner(
                CertificatePinner.Builder()
                    .add(CertificatePins.HOST, CertificatePins.CURRENT, CertificatePins.BACKUP)
                    .build()
            )
        }
    }
}
```

Verify: Put a proxy such as mitmproxy in front of the app and make the device trust its CA (§8.10, Verify it). Requests to the pinned host should fail on Android and on iOS.

Book: [§8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

## KMP-004: Ktor client logs headers or bodies in every build

Use `LogLevel.NONE` in release builds, and add `sanitizeHeader { it == HttpHeaders.Authorization }` wherever headers are logged.

```kotlin
install(Logging) {
    level = if (isDebugBuild) LogLevel.HEADERS else LogLevel.NONE
    sanitizeHeader { it == HttpHeaders.Authorization || it == HttpHeaders.Cookie }
}
```

Verify: Install a release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat` or Console.app: no `Authorization` header or response body should appear.

Book: [§6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

## KMP-005: Kotlin iOS code accepts any server certificate

Call `SecTrustEvaluateWithError` on `challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust` and cancel the challenge when it fails, or use Ktor's Darwin `CertificatePinner`, which validates the chain first.

```kotlin
handleChallenge { _, _, challenge, completionHandler ->
    val trust = challenge.protectionSpace.serverTrust
    if (trust != null && SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, null)) {
        completionHandler(NSURLSessionAuthChallengeUseCredential, NSURLCredential.create(trust = trust))
    } else {
        completionHandler(NSURLSessionAuthChallengeCancelAuthenticationChallenge, null)
    }
}
```

Verify: Route an iPhone through a proxy whose CA it doesn't trust; every request from the shared client should fail.

Book: [§8.10](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#810-how-to-implement-it)

## KMP-006: Shared settings library stores a token in plain storage

Put secrets behind an `expect` interface backed by `KeychainSettings` on Apple and a Keystore-backed store (Tink with DataStore) on Android. Keep only non-secret settings in plain storage.

```kotlin
// commonMain
interface SecretStore { fun put(key: String, value: String); fun get(key: String): String? }

// iosMain
class IosSecretStore : SecretStore {
    private val settings = KeychainSettings(service = "com.example.secrets")
    override fun put(key: String, value: String) = settings.putString(key, value)
    override fun get(key: String) = settings.getStringOrNull(key)
}
// androidMain: Tink AEAD with an android-keystore:// master key over DataStore (§6.6).
```

Verify: Sign in on an emulator and run `adb shell run-as <package> cat shared_prefs/*.xml`; no token or password should appear. On iOS, check the app's Preferences plist the same way.

Book: [§21.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#212-the-mistake-that-will-bite-you)
